clue.text: Events with food, involving skill

indicators.note: the food word wraps around, or involves, the skill word

parts.note: pies are food
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Gatherings where a meal is served and some talent is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties are social occasions, so they are events in the plural sense.

clue.text: Forwards? King's better going backwards

indicators.note: in this down clue the combined letters are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A paradox: the forwards are bettered by a king retreating.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the forwards are collectively the pack; the question mark flags that sporting sense. 'going backwards' turns KCAP round.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the eight forwards who scrum together are known as the pack.

clue.text: Marciano to lose his footing and sway from side to side

indicators.note: his footing is the foot, the last letter, of the boxer's name in this down clue, which is dropped

parts.note: Rocky Marciano was an undefeated American heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.surface: A boxer slips and staggers about the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocky Marciano was a famous American heavyweight; 'to lose his footing' drops the Y at the bottom of ROCKY.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to move gently back and forth, as a cradle or boat does.

clue.text: Computer system at home managed to be overloaded with tweets, oddly

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: the managing word is loaded within the letters taken from the tweets, which sit around it
take the odd-numbered letters of tweets

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A home network swamped by social media posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweets' suggests the internet, but 'oddly' only mines its odd letters, and 'to be overloaded with' means those letters carry the managing word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: An intranet is a private computer network used within one organisation.

clue.text: Half of nuclear power plant includes electron capture

indicators.note: the shortened name holds the electron symbol inside it
only the first half of the power station's name is kept, the rest being cut away

parts.note: Sizewell is a nuclear power station on the Suffolk coast of England
e is the physics symbol for an electron

explanation.surface: A physics note about a reactor trapping a particle.
explanation.walkthrough: Sizewell is a nuclear power station in Suffolk, England; 'Half of' leaves SIZE, which 'includes' E.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize something is to grab or take hold of it, a synonym of capture as a verb.

clue.text: Channel 50: see Doctor Who outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other pieces
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A TV listing: tune to channel 50 to watch Doctor Who.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges WHO to HOW, which goes 'outside' L and LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a groove or depression, so it can mean a channel cut into a surface.

clue.text: Conclusions of ball games being played

parts.note: O is shaped like a ball

indicators.note: the letters of the word are played around with, rearranged

explanation.surface: The final moments of matches in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball games' reads as one phrase, but 'ball' is the round letter and 'being played' jumbles only the games.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence an ending or conclusion.

clue.text: Oils (and even parts of flour) can fill us in the UK

indicators.note: the second and fourth letters of flour are taken
the container word goes inside the word for British people

parts.note: people in the UK call themselves Brits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cookery aside: oils, along with bits of flour, are going in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even parts of' takes the second and fourth letters; 'fill' puts the tin inside the Britons, so the bracket is wordplay, not an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubricants are oils and greases used to reduce friction, so oils is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Temperature was rising for antelopes in desolate areas

parts.note: the word was, rising in this down clue, climbs to sit above the temperature letter rather than after it
elands are large African antelopes

explanation.surface: Heat once drove antelope herds into barren terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' is not a reversal: Qaos meant WAS floats up like bubbles to sit above T in the down light, so the pieces simply read in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastelands are barren, unused tracts of land, which matches desolate areas.

clue.text: Around freezing, I talk nonsense to snowball?

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for around
0C, zero degrees Celsius, is freezing point

indicators.note: talking nonsense jumbles these letters

explanation.surface: Someone babbling about a cold drink at a chilly party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonsense' turns I TALK into KTAIL. A snowball is a drink of advocaat and lemonade; the question mark says it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowball is a mixed drink, so it is one example of a cocktail.

clue.text: Island the French shed tears over

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)

indicators.note: the word for crying is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry, shed tears

explanation.surface: French people wept over a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as 'about' in the surface but tells you to turn the crying word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesbos is a Greek island in the north-eastern Aegean Sea.

clue.text: WC Grace finally caught by child — outstanding 150!

indicators.note: the middle pieces are held inside the word for a small child

parts.note: a tot is a small child
read as 1 and 50: I and L in Roman numerals

indicators.note: take the last letter of Grace

explanation.surface: A cricket report: W.G. Grace caught by a youngster after a superb 150.
explanation.walkthrough: WC looks like the initials of W.G. Grace, the famous Victorian cricketer, but it is the definition. 150 is split into 1 and 50 as Roman numerals, and 'caught by' puts those plus the end of Grace inside the child.
explanation.definitionFit: WC, short for water closet, is a lavatory, a lavatory being a toilet.

clue.text: Play a trick on, as a chauffeur might do

definitions.meaning: to take someone for a ride is to deceive or con them
literally, a chauffeur takes passengers for a ride in a car

explanation.surface: A driver who fools their passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for cheating someone is also the literal job of a hired driver.

clue.text: Pod fell over, perhaps set here?

parts.note: a pod or school is a group of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: in this down clue the hill word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a fell is a moor or upland in northern England

explanation.surface: Something fell over, perhaps this is where it lay.
explanation.walkthrough: A set is a group of pupils grouped by ability, taught in a classroom; 'perhaps' and the question mark mark the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A school set, a class of pupils, would be taught in a schoolroom.

clue.text: Fit into Dot's building, otherwise it can stop the horses bolting

definitions.text: it can stop the horses bolting

indicators.note: the fitness word goes into the rearranged letters
the letters are built into a new arrangement

parts.note: able means fit, capable
or means otherwise, as in hurry or you'll miss it

explanation.surface: Instructions for fitting a door into Dot's barn to keep horses in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges Dot's to STDO and 'into' sets the fitness word inside it. The definition plays on the proverb about shutting the door after the horse has bolted.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable door, when shut, keeps the horses inside the stable.

clue.text: Halt! Sacred ground where many worship

indicators.note: ground means crushed and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sign at holy ground calling visitors to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' tempts as part of 'sacred ground', but it is the anagram signal for HALT SACRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathedrals are large churches, places where congregations gather to pray.

clue.text: Tolkien's half-elven lord cycles in verse

indicators.note: letters are cycled from the front of the name round to its end

parts.note: Elrond is the half-elven lord of Rivendell in Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings

explanation.surface: A fantasy elf goes cycling within a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycles' moves EL from the front of ELROND to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondel is a short poem with a fixed form and repeated lines, a kind of verse.

clue.text: Turkish commander's in range

definitions.meaning: a military commander or official in the Ottoman Empire
a brand of heavy cast-iron range cooker, common in British country kitchens

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer within firing distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga is both an Ottoman title and a well-known British make of kitchen stove.

clue.text: Groups of 4 or 2 pints best drunk without bottle-opener

parts.note: a quart is two pints

indicators.note: the remaining letters are drunk, reeling into a new order
the opener of bottle is its first letter, B, which is removed from the word best

explanation.surface: Drinkers sinking pints of the best, lacking a way to open bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle-opener' is the first letter of bottle, removed from best by 'without'; 'drunk' then rearranges what is left into ETS. A quart is two British pints.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartet is a group of four, often musicians, so quartets are groups of four.

clue.text: Relative travels around globe

indicators.note: the word goes around, turning back to front

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative

explanation.surface: A family member journeying round the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels around' turns BRO into ORB.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere, which is what a globe is.

clue.text: Taught in primary school to recall short father on the box

indicators.note: primary means first, so the first letter of school
to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: curt means short, brusque
Father Ted is a television sitcom about an Irish priest; the box is TV

explanation.surface: A child learning from a TV priest while at junior school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recall' turns CURT into TRUC. Father Ted is a 1990s British-Irish TV comedy, so the father on the box is TED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be instructed is to be taught, both past participles of teaching.

clue.text: One being advised when workers gain support

parts.note: men are workers, as in management and men
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Employees get backing when they take counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentee is someone guided by a mentor, a person receiving advice.

clue.text: Readers of stories?

parts.note: stories here are lies, and readers are instruments that read or detect them, not people reading books

explanation.surface: People who read tales, as in a book club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stories' means fibs and 'readers' are machines that read them.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph detects lies, so it reads the truth of stories told.

clue.text: Somewhat controversial treasure

indicators.note: somewhat means part of, so the letters lie within the next word

explanation.surface: A disputed hoard of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove, as in treasure trove, is a store of valuables found.

clue.text: 4 in favour of stealing uranium

indicators.note: the support word takes in the element symbol, as if stealing it

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in for the motion
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A vote cast for nuclear theft.
explanation.definitionFit: The numeral 4 is written as the number word.

clue.text: For a long time, salaries drop 20%

indicators.note: drop means lose, so a portion of the pay word is taken away

parts.note: wages are salaries, pay
one letter out of five is twenty per cent, here the first letter of the pay word

explanation.surface: Pay has fallen by a fifth over a long spell.
explanation.walkthrough: One letter is 20% of WAGES; 'drop 20%' loses the W.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal idiom for a long time, as in waiting for ages.

clue.text: Old ship builder bites tip of tongue, having sworn

indicators.note: the builder's name closes around the tongue's tip as if biting it

parts.note: Noah built the ark

indicators.note: the tip is the first letter of tongue

explanation.surface: An aged boatwright bites his tongue after swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bites' puts T inside ONOAH, before its final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given on oath is given after swearing to tell the truth.

clue.text: Solve cryptic by working with Guardian's first serenade

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: on means working, as in the machine is on

indicators.note: take the first letter of Guardian

explanation.surface: Solving a Guardian cryptic as a romantic act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges SOLVE to LOVES, then ON and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song, sung or played to a beloved.

clue.text: Put half your money to begin with on red, returning to make a killing

indicators.note: the first letter of money is taken, and it also goes at the start
the last half of your is taken
the colour is turned back, read backwards

explanation.surface: A roulette bet: stake half your cash on red to win big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes UR from your, and 'returning' turns RED into DER. Reversed, the whole word is REDRUM, as in The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: To murder is to kill, and 'make a killing' read literally means commit a killing.

clue.text: Makes certain to blame son if cocaine goes missing

indicators.note: the drug letter disappears from the combined word

parts.note: to censure is to blame or criticise
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Pinning the blame on a son once drugs vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes missing' removes C from CENSURES.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, a straight synonym in the third person.
